research.title: Predictive Calibration Under Covariate Shift
bullets: Designed experiments with supervisor guidance to compare probability calibration methods under controlled covariate shifts in synthetic and tabular classification datasets.
Evaluated temperature scaling and isotonic regression using held-out calibration sets, reliability diagrams, and bootstrap intervals across varying training sample sizes.

work.title: Data Validation and Batch Processing
bullets: Implemented Python validation routines for incoming transaction records, checking schema consistency, missing fields, and duplicate identifiers before downstream batch processing.
Maintained automated tests for parsing and transformation logic, investigated failed batch runs, and documented error handling behavior for recurring input issues.

projects.title: Regularization for Correlated Regression Predictors
bullets: Implemented ridge, lasso, and elastic net regression comparisons on synthetic datasets with correlated predictors and varying levels of observation noise.
Used nested cross-validation to select regularization parameters and compared prediction error, coefficient stability, and variable selection behavior across repeated data splits.

projects.title: Density Estimation for Multimodal Data
bullets: Implemented kernel density estimation and Gaussian mixture model baselines for synthetic distributions exhibiting skewness, overlapping modes, and unequal component variances.
Compared bandwidth and component selection strategies using validation likelihood, inspecting fitted densities to characterize oversmoothing and sensitivity to mixture initialization.

projects.title: Prediction Intervals with Split Conformal Regression
bullets: Implemented split conformal prediction around linear regression and random forest baselines, separating model fitting, calibration, and evaluation data to prevent leakage.
Compared empirical coverage and interval width under homoscedastic and heteroscedastic noise, examining how aggregate coverage concealed variation across input regions.
